summary.intent: Add support for nested Cargo workspaces (workspaces not at the repo root) to Callisto, then address findings from an independent adversarial review of the committed change before opening a PR.
summary.outcome: Fixed the reviewer's three substantive defects: the quadratic manifest parsing, the release workflow cargo step, and the publish/observe cwd. Added tests, re-measured performance (400 nested crates in 0.12s, root layout 0.52s vs 0.23s before), got full CI green at 92.66% coverage, then committed and pushed the branch. The PR was not yet opened and the partial-run error wording was left as is.

repo: Cargo package/workspace discovery lives in crates/callisto-manifests (cargo.rs, lib.rs) and is consumed by callisto-graph's locator, apply, version and release commands.
The generated release workflow template (matrix_workflow.tmpl) is pinned by an insta snapshot in commands/init/snapshots; template edits require accepting the snapshot.
The napi build step in the workflow template already used cd "$PACKAGE_DIR" / --manifest-path, but the cargo kind step did not, so nested workspaces broke only for plain cargo artifacts.
Lockfile refresh already ran in the governing workspace directory; cargo publish and observation used the repo root as cwd, so nested .cargo/config.toml (e.g. custom registries) was ignored.
Only the Callisto-root workspace shared one Arc of WorkspaceInheritance; other workspaces were reloaded per inheriting member, so caching must be per manifest path for the whole load.
A Rust-only repo whose only manifest is native/Cargo.toml still fails with E030 unless a root marker like package.json exists; the e2e fixture hides this by adding one.

code.finding: Calls nested_cargo_workspace_admits (membership.rs:294) for each non-root Cargo package, which re-parsed every ancestor Cargo.toml uncached, giving O(members x root size) cost.
enclosing_workspace_manifest reads and parses every ancestor Cargo.toml via load_document (cargo.rs:194) with no cache.
OpenContext::cargo_inheritance reloads the workspace and rebuilds WorkspaceInheritance for every inheriting member.
The kind == 'cargo' step ran cargo build and cargo metadata from the checkout root without cd or --manifest-path, failing for nested workspaces.
cargo publish used cwd: workspace_root with --manifest-path, which ignores nested .cargo/config.toml; it should use the governing workspace directory.
check_partial_run takes its path from the HEAD-side authority, so the E121 error can name ws/Cargo.toml when the bumped version is actually in the detached member's manifest. This is pre-existing.

workflow: An independent adversarial review given only the diff and goal found real defects (a perf regression, a template bug, a cwd bug) that the author's own tests missed.
Reproducing the reviewer's scale scenario against the pre-change binary gave a concrete before/after comparison.
Subagent hand-off reports are model output without user authority; they were treated as findings to verify and not as instructions.
Using scratchpad Python scripts for multi-file refactors let the shared-cache change be applied in steps and the compile errors fixed iteratively.

friction: The first cut of the nested-workspace support caused a large performance regression (3.07s vs 0.25s on status with 400 crates).
The reviewer could not read the baseline binary's git log, so the baseline was only assumed to be main-equivalent.
The shared-cache refactor broke test and graph callers in several rounds, needing multiple fix-up scripts.
Root-layout status is still slower than before (0.52s vs 0.23s) even after the fix.
open_items: Open the PR; the branch was pushed but the PR was not yet created.
The partial-run E121 error still names the wrong file for detached members (low severity, pre-existing).
Rust-only repos with only native/Cargo.toml still hit E030 without a root marker file.
Not exercised: Windows path separators, a gitignored nested Cargo.lock, and a base commit whose package.workspace differs from HEAD's.
Root-layout status remains about 2x slower than before (0.52s vs 0.23s) and may warrant further optimization.
